ideas.description: Exploit: remove more high-resolution backward work, extending E029. On E030 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 0.7533 @ 6.95 s), freeze the whole first group-1 conv block (conv 32x32 whitening-output -> 128, pool, BN, GELU) during the 4 epochs at 32 px. In the 32 px CUDA graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv, and drop that conv's weight and its BN affine params from that phase's Muon/SGD parameter lists (or zero their LR). E029 already skips this conv's dgrad. This change also removes its wgrad at 32x32 and the BN/GELU/pool backward at 32x32 and 16x16. BN stays in train mode, so running stats keep updating at 32 px. Capture the modified 32 px graph in build, keeping the same graph count with no recapture in the timed region. Log ms/step per phase. Rationale (FreezeOut-style): the first conv sees the whitened patches and converges earliest. The 28 px and 20/24 px phases (7 epochs) still train it.
ideas.expected: 32 px ms/step falls 5-9%, so total time falls about 0.15-0.25 s (-2 to -3.5%), to about 6.7-6.8 s. Accuracy -0.0 to -0.3 pp versus the pooled ~0.753, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=1.5% lower; also run a salt-1 companion if it lands within 0.1 pp of the bar. If accuracy falls >=0.3 pp, conv1 still needs full-res updates: try freezing only during the last 2 epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit: cut Muon's fixed per-step cost (about 1.5 ms of ~350 steps, roughly 7% of train time) once more. On E030, keep Turbo/AOL column preconditioning but run 1 Newton-Schulz quintic step instead of 2. Use the same coefficients, the same lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, and the per-step weight renorm unchanged. Recapture all 4 graphs in build. Rationale: E024 showed Muon is insensitive to singular-value spread in [0.67, 1.2], and E028 showed accuracy is flat in lr over 0.205-0.256. The per-step renorm also fixes the overall update scale, so a less exact orthogonalization may cost nothing. Log Muon ms/step.
ideas.expected: Muon time drops about 0.2-0.3 ms/step, so time falls about 0.07-0.1 s (-1 to -1.5%), to about 6.85-6.88 s. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp of the pooled ~0.753. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.753 and time is >=0.8% lower. If accuracy falls >=0.3 pp, 2 NS steps is the floor; close the NS-step axis for H2.5.2.

ideas.description: Rebase of I039 onto the current incumbent, for calibration and a safe-margin fallback. On E030, add 0.5 epoch at 32 px (2x20+3x24+2x28+4.5x32, LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps) and change nothing else. A 0.5-epoch step is about 2x the trajectory noise, so its effect can be read. It fixes the pp/s line at the 32 px end for scoring per-step cuts. It also gives the config to submit if the official 40-seed mean of E030 looks marginal.
ideas.expected: Time +0.40-0.43 s (about 7.36 s). Accuracy +0.35 to +0.6 pp, about 0.757-0.759, a slope of 0.8-1.4 pp/s. This won't beat E030 on time, so log it as calibration (discard). If the gain is <0.25 pp, the 32 px tail is saturating; margin must then come from lr/schedule, and per-step cuts are worth less than assumed.

ideas.description: Explore which pixels buy margin most cheaply, as a companion to the rebased I039. On E030, add one extra 20 px epoch at the start (3x20+3x24+2x28+4x32, 12 epochs, LR triangle and Lookahead over total steps; same 20 px graph, no new shapes). Change nothing else. The 20 px epoch is the cheapest epoch (~0.43 s), and E031 showed that early-phase optimizer step count matters under Muon. So extra early steps may buy as much accuracy per second as the 32 px tail at roughly equal cost.
ideas.expected: Time +0.42-0.45 s (about 7.38 s). Accuracy +0.15 to +0.5 pp, centred near +0.3 pp. If its gain is >= the +0.5 epoch at 32 px run (I039 rebased) at equal time, low-res epochs are the cheaper margin source: future margin top-ups should be low-res epochs, and the 32 px phase can be trimmed (see the 28 px shift idea). If the gain is <0.15 pp, early epochs are saturated and margin must come from the 32 px end.

ideas.description: Exploit and test the FixRes mechanism: the closing full-res phase only needs to re-fit BN stats and the head, so it can be shorter. On the current incumbent (E030, or the low-res-epoch variant if that run is kept), move one 32 px epoch to 28 px: 2x20+3x24+3x28+3x32 (11 epochs, same LR schedule over total steps, same 4 graphs). Change nothing else. Run salt 0 and salt 1 and compare against the pooled estimate, since the expected effect is near the noise.
ideas.expected: Time -0.17 to -0.2 s (a 28 px epoch costs ~0.66 s vs ~0.84 s at 32 px), to about 6.75-6.8 s (-2.5%). Accuracy -0.0 to -0.25 pp, centred near -0.1 pp. Keep it if the 2-salt mean is >=0.753. If the loss is <=0.1 pp, H2.3.2 is supported and a 2x32 px tail is next. If the loss is >=0.3 pp, the 32 px phase is doing feature learning, not just BN re-fitting; refute H2.3.2.

ideas.description: Rebase of I040 onto the current incumbent. On E030, raise label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.4 in all phases and change nothing else. ls is a graph constant, so recapture all 4 graphs in build. E012 (0.3 -> 0.2 lost 0.21 pp) suggests the optimum may sit at or above 0.3 for 100 classes in an under-fit 11-epoch schedule. This is the last untested direction of the ls knob, and it is time-free.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.15 to +0.25 pp, weak prior near +0.1 pp. Keep it only if the 3-seed mean is >=0.755 (+0.2 pp over the pooled ~0.753), then spend the margin on a time cut (freeze conv1, 28 px shift). A drop of >=0.15 pp closes the ls axis at 0.3.

ideas.description: Explore an untested Muon knob: momentum. E028 showed lr is flat over 0.205-0.256, but momentum 0.655 is inherited from Hiverge's CIFAR-10 3/3/3 net without resizing or AOL. On E030, raise the Muon momentum from 0.655 to 0.75 (Nesterov form unchanged) and keep lr, the SGD groups, the schedule, Lookahead and resolutions fixed. Momentum is a graph constant, so recapture all graphs in build. Rationale: E031 showed the early phase is step-limited; higher momentum smooths the orthogonalized direction across consecutive small-batch steps, which may raise per-step progress.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.25 to +0.3 pp, no strong prior. Keep it if the 3-seed mean is >=0.755 (a salt-1 companion is required if it lands in 0.753-0.755). If it falls >=0.2 pp, try 0.55 next only if the drop is large (>=0.4 pp); otherwise close the momentum axis.

drop.reason: Based on E025, which is superseded by E030 (20 px start plus the whitening detach). It is re-queued as the same +0.5 epoch at 32 px calibration on E030, so the measured slope applies to the current recipe.
Based on E025, which is superseded by E030. It is re-queued unchanged (ls 0.4) on E030, with the keep bar raised to 0.755 because the expected accuracy of the incumbent is about at the 0.753 bar.

structured_output.summary:
The incumbent is E030: 0.7533 in 6.95 s. Its expected accuracy, from the pooled E025/E027 calibration, sits right at the 0.753 bar, so any time cut needs either extra margin or a near-zero accuracy cost.

I dropped I039 and I040 because both were built on E025, which E030 has replaced. Both are re-queued unchanged on E030.

The new queue has 7 ideas. Four are exploits:
- **Freeze group-1 conv in the 32 px phase (H2.4, priority 4):** freeze the first group-1 conv block during the 32 px epochs. This removes its 32x32 weight-gradient and BN backward work. Expected about -2 to -3.5% time.
- **1 Newton-Schulz step after AOL (H2.5.2, priority 3):** expected about -1 to -1.5% time.
- **Move one 32 px epoch to 28 px (H2.3.2, priority 3):** tests whether the closing 32 px phase only needs to re-fit BN and the head. Run with 2 salts; expected about -2.5% time.
- **+0.5 epoch at 32 px on E030 (H1.8.1, priority 4):** calibrates the accuracy-per-second slope and gives a safe-margin fallback config.

Three are explores, each meant to add margin:
- **One extra 20 px epoch (H1.8, priority 3):** compares the cheapest epoch against the 32 px tail as a way to buy margin.
- **Label smoothing 0.4 (H1.3.1, priority 2):** the last untested direction of the label-smoothing knob.
- **Muon momentum 0.75 (H1.7, priority 2):** momentum is untested, while lr is already known to be flat.

Margin-adding runs can't be kept on time alone. Their job is to set the exchange rate between accuracy and time, and to say which margin source should pair with the time cuts.
